properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation seated upon Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Strathclyde Group (sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone formations overlain by dense glacial till). Superstructure masonry composed predominantly of Carboniferous Craigleith Sandstone—a fine-to-medium-grained, quartz-cemented pale buff-to-grey arenite prized for exceptional compressive strength and weathering resistance. Secondary structural walling and rear elevations employ coursed Hailes Sandstone rubble with a higher mica and clay content. Mortar matrices consist of traditional non-hydraulic to feebly hydraulic lime blended with sharp, poorly sorted river sand aggregate. Subterranean urban drainage channels into historical culverts beneath the bedrock interface.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Peripheral urban specimens (*Acer pseudoplatanus* - Sycamore, and *Tilia × europaea* - Common Lime). Late-June phenological state: dense, fully expanded chlorophyll-saturated foliage forming closed, heavy, convex crown volumes with deep emerald-green palmate and cordate leaf structures; vigorous summer shoot extension with zero defoliation.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical civic monumental core (St George's Church / West Register House, designed by Robert Reid after Robert Adam) defined by a central colossal tetrastyle Roman Ionic portico recessed between projecting rusticated outer pavilions with arched niches. Above the attic level rises a high circular drum with a peristyle colonnade supporting a prominent ribbed spherical dome and cupola finial. Flanking the monument are unified Class-A listed Georgian residential and institutional terraces (three storeys over rusticated basements and attic tiers). Facades feature strict vertical alignment: channelled rusticated ground floors, smooth ashlar upper tiers, 6-over-6 and 12-pane timber sash-and-case windows, continuous string courses, moulded entablatures, and balustraded parapets. Roofs are hipped and pitched with lead-lined valleys, flat asphalt pavilion crowns, and coped ashlar party-wall chimney stacks bearing cylindrical terracotta cans.
